subject: Performance SLO follow-up: p95/p99 end-to-end latency (hosted vs current provider)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>

Subject: Performance SLO follow-up: p95/p99 end-to-end latency (hosted vs current provider)

Hi Elena / Mike 

Great to talk earlier  thanks for walking us through the Finlytics production flow and the perf targets you need to hit. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

Recap (from the call):
- Primary goal: match or improve your current end-to-end latency SLOs for inference on user queries (including network, request/response handling, model inference).
- Target workloads: interactive analytics UI (avg response payload ~350 tokens), some batch scoring for alerts (longer payloads sporadic).
- Streaming: client wants token-by-token streaming for the analytics UI to render partial results.
- Current provider: you mentioned some variance at load  details below in your reply.

What we heard for SLOs (please confirm):
- p95 end-to-end (user -> response complete) target: <= 250 ms for 350-token responses (interactive UI).
- p99 end-to-end target: <= 600 ms for same payload.
- Sustained concurrency target: ~60-100 concurrent users during peak (approx 80 CCU).
- Throughput target: ~180 QPS at 1.5s avg request time (as a ballpark for sizing).

Next steps (recommended):
1) Aditya to provide a short latency profile for Redwood hosted for similar workloads (p50/p95/p99 numbers with and without streaming enabled).
2) Exchange a small test harness (we can run a short A/B with a synthetic trace or replay ~30 minutes).
3) If numbers look good, scope a short pilot with traffic mirroring for 48 hours.

I attached a one-page SLO summary and a simple latency worksheet so we can capture exact payload sizes and concurrency assumptions.

If the targets above are off, let us know and we'll adjust. Would you be available for a 30-min technical sync tomorrow (Fri) at 10:30am PT? If not, propose a time and we'll do our best to accommodate.

Thanks 

Marissa Cole

marissa@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0123

From: Elena Soto <elena@finlytics.ai>

Subject: Re: Performance SLO follow-up: p95/p99 end-to-end latency (hosted vs current provider)

Thanks Marissa  that summary is spot on. A couple clarifications and current numbers from our side: 

Clarifications:
- The 350-token number is average for interactive queries; we occasionally see 700+ token queries for deep analysis but those are ~5% of traffic.
- Streaming: we need first-token within 100ms of request start for a good UX, then steady streaming thereafter.

Current provider observed (production, last 30 days):
- p50: 220 ms
- p95: 480 ms
- p99: 1.2 s
- Tail variability increases during peak spikes (we saw p99 spike to ~1.6s during an incident last month).
- Sustained concurrency: spikes to 120 CCU for short windows; average peak ~85 CCU.

We can provide a small replay trace (anonymized) and give a 48-hour window where we can mirror traffic to a test endpoint. We prefer to do a non-prod mirror first.

Mike and I are available tomorrow at 10:30am PT for the technical sync. Looking forward to the numbers from Aditya.

Elena
Elena Soto
Head of Product Engineering | Finlytics
elena@finlytics.ai

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Soto <elena@finlytics.ai>, Mike Chen <mike.chen@finlytics.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 16 Jul 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Performance SLO follow-up: p95/p99 end-to-end latency (hosted vs current provider)

Hi Elena / Mike 

Thanks for the details and the replay offer  that's perfect. A few notes from the engineering side based on the workload you described, plus some numbers from recent similar pilots: 

Redwood hosted (baseline configuration we typically use for interactive workloads):
- Test profile: 350-token avg response, batching disabled for low latency interactive path, streaming enabled.
- Observed (from a 30-min synthetic replay at ~180 QPS, 80 concurrency):
  - p50: ~120 ms (end-to-end)
  - p95: ~180 ms (end-to-end)
  - p99: ~420 ms (end-to-end)
- First-token latency (stream enabled): median ~40-60 ms; 95th ~90-110 ms depending on client handshake and network.

Notes and assumptions:
- Our numbers include model execution and the typical networking overhead within the hosted region (us-west). They assume moderately sized models (7-13B) on optimized kernels. Larger models will increase numbers; we can map exact model profiles during the pilot.
- Sustained concurrency: our dedicated pools can sustain 200+ concurrent streams with predictable tail latencies; the hosted multi-tenant fleet also supports your stated CCU but for the tightest p99 you'd want either a reserved pool or guidance on autoscale policies (we can propose a dedicated slot in the pilot).

Recommended technical next steps:
1) Share the anonymized replay trace and a 48-hour mirror window. We'll run a parallel replay against a Redwood test endpoint and produce p50/p95/p99 and first-token latency histograms.
2) We'll instrument streaming delivery to show chunk latency (first-token and inter-token gaps).
3) If you want, we can provision a short dedicated test pool (48 hours) so you're seeing conservative numbers that match committed capacity.

I'll attach a raw CSV latency sample and a simple workbook (redwood-hosted-latency-sheet.xlsx) so you can compare apples-to-apples.

Do you want me to provision the mirror endpoint now or wait until after the sync?

Cheers,
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.ai
